note: Nothing here is closed by editing one side to agree with the other. Conflicts are recorded and traceable.

conflicts.about: the Skill label printed on all 102 pages of the S-004/S-005 block against what the items test
conflicts.statement_a: every page of the block prints Domain "Advanced Math" and Skill "Equivalent expressions", across both files
conflicts.statement_b: 16 of the 102 test exponent rules or radicals, 10 manipulate rational expressions, 10 are one- or two-step linear collections
conflicts.why: the label is uniform across a block whose contents are not; 26 are coded to another topic and the 10 rational ones need a KDG node the Polynomials mapping does not carry
conflicts.resolution: NONE. The label is preserved verbatim as observed_topic and source_label; the coded topic is separate and neither is edited to agree.

conflicts.about: whether the S-004/S-005 block is Digital SAT material at all
conflicts.statement_a: every page prints Assessment "SAT" and the question-bank field layout, and the bank carries Digital SAT items
conflicts.statement_b: 17 items across the block refer to a stimulus printed "above" them, the pre-2024 paper layout; the Digital SAT wording is "the given expression"
conflicts.why: the metadata does not distinguish the paper SAT from the Digital SAT, and the wording points the other way for part of the block
conflicts.resolution: NONE. Provenance stays "unknown" with confidence UNKNOWN, and generation_eligibility stays NOT_DIRECT_SOURCE. The observation is recorded on the affected records.

conflicts.about: block A is headed "Polynomials" and contains an item that is not one
conflicts.statement_a: S-003 is headed "Polynomials" and every item in it is filed under that heading
conflicts.statement_b: the item on page 1 numbered 2 is an exponential model recovered from a three-row table
conflicts.why: a topic heading applied to a compiled set is a filing decision, not a property of each item in it
conflicts.resolution: NONE. observed_topic stays "polynomials" as the source has it; the coded topic is Exponential Functions and the record carries SOURCE_CONFLICT.

conflicts.about: a constant named in a stem that does not appear in the printed function (S-003 page 3 item 12)
conflicts.statement_a: the stem says three constants are involved
conflicts.statement_b: the printed function contains only two of them; the parallel item on page 4 prints the third as a leading scalar
conflicts.why: the compilation appears to have dropped a symbol in transcription, which changes what the item asks
conflicts.resolution: NONE. Recorded on the record as observed. The item is not repaired: this knowledge base records what the source says, and a silent correction would erase the evidence that this source can drop a symbol.

conflicts.about: an unstated multiplicity that the stated answer depends on (S-003 page 5 item 27)
conflicts.statement_a: the item divides a function by a linear factor at one of its x-intercepts and asks for the resulting count
conflicts.statement_b: the count follows only if that intercept has multiplicity one, which the source never states
conflicts.why: the answer key gives a single value, so the source treats an unstated assumption as given
conflicts.resolution: NONE. Recorded on the record as observed; the archetype notes the dependence.

conflicts.about: the answer key on S-005 pages 54-56 was produced through a spreadsheet and is machine-mangled
conflicts.statement_a: the key lists 102 rows as Number / ID / Answer, matching both files in page order
conflicts.statement_b: one ID is destroyed by scientific-notation autoformatting and two answers are truncated to a bare decimal point
conflicts.why: a hex id that reads as a number was reformatted, so the key cannot be joined on ID alone without repairing it
conflicts.resolution: NONE. The key is not stored in this repository and no id is corrected in it. The affected row is recoverable only by page position, which is recorded here and nowhere relied on.

conflicts.about: the section heading "Linear System of Equations" over items that are not linear systems
conflicts.statement_a: S-006 is headed "Linear System of Equations" and its answer key repeats that heading
conflicts.statement_b: 3 of the 86 items pair a line with a parabola, so the system is not linear
conflicts.why: a heading applied to a compiled section is a filing decision, not a property of each item under it
conflicts.resolution: NONE. observed_topic stays the source heading; those records also carry ALG_010 and N-QUAD, and the mismatch is declared.

conflicts.about: option-letter labelling is inconsistent within S-006
conflicts.statement_a: the set labels choices A) B) C) D) throughout
conflicts.statement_b: one item runs A) B) C) E) with no D, and two items parenthesise the letters as (A) (B) (C) (D)
conflicts.why: the letters are transcription, not content, but a missing D means one printed choice cannot be selected as written
conflicts.resolution: NONE. Recorded on the affected records. No letter is corrected: the KB stores no option letters at all, and repairing the source would hide that this compiler mis-transcribes.

conflicts.about: the circles file is named for 50 questions and contains 47
conflicts.statement_a: the filename reads "Circles 50 REAL QUESTION WITH ANS KEY"
conflicts.statement_b: the document numbers its items 1 to 47, and the printed answer key has 47 rows
conflicts.why: a count in a filename is not evidence about the document, and here the two disagree by three
conflicts.resolution: NONE. 47 records were coded, one per numbered item. The filename count is recorded on the source row as filename_claims and is not used anywhere.

conflicts.about: the exam-topic axis has no row reaching "Solid Geometry"
conflicts.statement_a: taxonomy.core.js has GEO_007 Solid Geometry and the KDG has N-SOLID
conflicts.statement_b: no exam topic in artifact 01 maps to either, so a three-dimensional item has no exam-topic home
conflicts.why: the eight existing taxonomy conflicts are the exam axis being FINER than the taxonomy; this is the axis missing a row the taxonomy has, which is the opposite direction
conflicts.resolution: NONE. taxonomy.core.js is frozen and artifact 01 records what its source said. The 43 three-dimensional items are filed under the nearest exam topic and every one declares both a topic and a KDG conflict.

conflicts.about: the solid-geometry file is named for 71 questions and contains 72
conflicts.statement_a: the filename reads "Solid Geomtry 71 Real Question"
conflicts.statement_b: the document numbers its items 1 to 72 with no gap or repeat, and the key has 72 rows
conflicts.why: the second filename count in two files to disagree with the document, this one in the opposite direction from the circles file
conflicts.resolution: NONE. 72 records were coded, one per numbered item. The filename count is recorded on the source row and used nowhere.

conflicts.about: the section carries two headings and the answer key repeats only one
conflicts.statement_a: the section is headed "Areas&Volumes" and, on the next line, "Solid Geomtry"
conflicts.statement_b: the answer key is headed "Answers: Areas&Volumes" alone, and the second heading is misspelled in both places
conflicts.why: the two names describe different scopes: roughly half the items are plane areas and perimeters, not solids
conflicts.resolution: NONE. Both headings are recorded in OBSERVED_TOPICS and the record carries the first; neither is corrected.

conflicts.about: items needing exam topic "Triangles" and exam topic "Geometry (Lines & Angles)" at once
conflicts.statement_a: the exam-topic axis gives each its own row, and each maps cleanly to one frozen subtopic
conflicts.statement_b: 11 items chase an angle through crossing lines INTO a triangle, so neither row alone holds them
conflicts.why: the axis assumes an item has one topic. These have two, and the tie is not a finer distinction but a genuine union, so no split of either row would fix it
conflicts.resolution: NONE. Each is filed on the row that carries the harder half and tagged with both subtopics, which raises TOPIC_CLASSIFICATION_CONFLICT on the record. The topic rows are not edited.

conflicts.about: the origin claimed for the 79 items of the S-010 block
conflicts.statement_a: the filename calls them a QUESTION BANK, which in this corpus has meant an official bank export
conflicts.statement_b: the pages carry an eight-character item id and nothing else
conflicts.why: the two earlier bank exports (S-002, S-004/S-005) printed Assessment, Test, Domain, Skill and Difficulty on every page. This block prints none of them, so the claim rests on the filename alone
conflicts.resolution: NONE. S-010 keeps provenance unknown at UNKNOWN confidence and generation_eligibility NOT_DIRECT_SOURCE. The filename claim is recorded, not believed.

conflicts.about: the topic the file claims against the topics its items test
conflicts.statement_a: the file is titled Triangles and block A carries the section heading "Triangles"
conflicts.statement_b: 34 of the 143 items are coded away from Triangles — 30 to Geometry (Lines & Angles) and 3 to Polygons, with 33 of the 34 in block B
conflicts.why: block B is a wider bank than the title admits: roughly a third of it is the parallel-lines and transversal construction, which block A never uses once
conflicts.resolution: NONE. The heading is preserved as observed_topic for block A; block B observes UNKNOWN. The coded topic is separate from both and neither is edited to agree.

conflicts.about: standard deviation, which the exam topic "Interquartile Range" is made to carry
conflicts.statement_a: the exam-topic axis has Mean, Median, Mode and Interquartile Range, and no topic for standard deviation
conflicts.statement_b: eight items in S-011 test standard deviation directly, comparing spread between distributions
conflicts.why: the only spread topic on the axis names a different statistic. STA_003 "Range & Interval" and N-SPREAD do cover it, so the frozen taxonomy is fine; the EXAM axis is what has no home
conflicts.resolution: NONE. The eight are filed on Interquartile Range with STA_003 and N-SPREAD, which is where spread lives, and this records that the topic name is wrong for them.

conflicts.about: the printed answer for item 34 of S-011
conflicts.statement_a: the key on page 17 gives D, which is 9.5
conflicts.statement_b: the table gives five times of 8, 6, 14, 11 and 11, whose mean is 10 — option B
conflicts.why: derived with exact arithmetic and checked against a render of both the item and the key page. No reading of the five rows produces 9.5
conflicts.resolution: NONE. The record carries the source key unchanged and an observed note that it is wrong. The compiler is not corrected, only contradicted on the record.

conflicts.about: what the S-011 filename and heading count and name
conflicts.statement_a: the file is named "42 Real Questions" and headed "Mean, Median, Mode, Range"
conflicts.statement_b: it holds 49 numbered items, its key stops at 42, no item asks for a mode, and eight test standard deviation
conflicts.why: the filename counts the KEY rather than the questions, and the heading names one measure the items never use while omitting the one eight of them turn on
conflicts.resolution: NONE. The heading is preserved as observed_topic and source_label; items 43-49 are recorded as beyond the key rather than dropped.

conflicts.about: the printed answer for item 62 of S-012
conflicts.statement_a: the key on page 14 gives 90
conflicts.statement_b: prey end at 28 times start, predators at 2.8 times start, so prey is 900% greater
conflicts.why: "increased by 2,700%" makes the end 28 times the start, and "p% greater than" divides by the SECOND quantity. 90 is what dividing by the larger count gives. Checked against a render of page 11
conflicts.resolution: NONE. The record keeps the source key and notes that it is wrong.

conflicts.about: the printed answer for item 67 of S-012
conflicts.statement_a: the key on page 14 gives B, which is 493
conflicts.statement_b: the residents who voted total 425,779 over 1,949 square miles, which is 218 — option C
conflicts.why: 493 is the prose population of 960,000 per square mile, ignoring the words "who voted". Three of the four options are the same division under a different numerator, and the key took one of the traps
conflicts.resolution: NONE. The record keeps the source key and notes that it is wrong.

conflicts.about: what the S-012 filename and heading count and name
conflicts.statement_a: the file is named "66 Real Questions" and headed "Percent; Ratio & Proportion"
conflicts.statement_b: it holds 67 numbered items, its key covers all 67, and one of them is a radical-to-exponent item
conflicts.why: the count is one short of the document and of its own key. Item 23 asks for the exponent form of a square root and belongs to neither named topic
conflicts.resolution: NONE. All 67 are coded; item 23 is filed on Exponential Functions where the exponents pilot filed its radicals, which raises the record-level conflicts that mapping already carries.

conflicts.about: exam topic "Trigonometry", which artifact 01 lists for ST1 and NOT for the DSAT
conflicts.statement_a: DSAT_TOPICS has 22 entries and no Trigonometry; ST1_TOPICS has 25 and does
conflicts.statement_b: S-013 is 24 items headed Trigonometry, every one tagged to a named DSAT administration
conflicts.why: the DSAT list folds trigonometry into Triangles, which is why that row alone carries GEO_005 and N-TRIG. The omission is a modelling choice, not a claim that the DSAT does not test it
conflicts.resolution: NONE, and none needed in the data: the 24 are filed under Triangles with GEO_005 and N-TRIG, which raises no record-level conflict. Recorded so the next DSAT trigonometry file does not repeat the investigation.

conflicts.about: the species count stated in item 17 of S-014
conflicts.statement_a: the stem says the researcher measured 34 different species
conflicts.statement_b: the table sums to 29 in both directions, and prints 29 as its own total
conflicts.why: the table is internally consistent — rows 3, 20, 6 and columns 6, 19, 4, 0 both give 29 — so the stem is the part that disagrees. Four other tables in this file sum exactly
conflicts.resolution: NONE. The item is coded and the discrepancy recorded; it does not change the answer, which conditions on two rows and never uses the total.

conflicts.about: the item count claimed by the S-014 filename
conflicts.statement_a: the file is named "18 Real Questions"
conflicts.statement_b: it holds 19 numbered items with no gaps, and its key covers all 19
conflicts.why: the second file in this corpus to undercount by exactly one, after S-012 claimed 66 of 67
conflicts.resolution: NONE. All 19 are coded; the claim is recorded on the source row as filename_claims.

conflicts.about: the printed answer for item 16 of S-015
conflicts.statement_a: the key on page 6 gives A, which is 0
conflicts.statement_b: 1.1 metres per second squared is 2.5 miles per minute squared — option B
conflicts.why: four sibling items in the same file use the identical conversion and their keys are all right; only this one is not. Zero is what inverting the squared time factor gives. Checked against a render
conflicts.resolution: NONE. The record keeps the source key and notes that it is wrong.

conflicts.about: what the S-015 filename counts and names
conflicts.statement_a: the file is named Units_24
conflicts.statement_b: it is headed Unit Conversion, holds 25 items, and one of them is a conditional probability
conflicts.why: the third file here to undercount by exactly one, after S-012 and S-014. Item 19 is the same construction as item 5 of S-014 and groups with it across the two files
conflicts.resolution: NONE. All 25 are coded; item 19 is filed under Probability with the archetype the probability corpus defined, which is how the cross-file duplicate surfaced.

conflicts.about: what the S-016/S-017 filename names
conflicts.statement_a: the file is named LINESANGLES_140_REAL_QUESTIONS
conflicts.statement_b: 36 of its 140 items are Geometry (Lines & Angles); block B is 12 per cent lines and angles, 25 items of solid geometry and 35 involving similarity, under its own heading "16 Geometry"
conflicts.why: the same title-versus-content pattern as S-009/S-010, and visible here in the file itself: the two blocks carry DIFFERENT headings, and block B’s names the content correctly while the filename does not
conflicts.resolution: NONE. Block A observes lines_and_angles and block B observes geometry, each from its own printed heading; every item is filed on what it tests.

conflicts.about: whether the file holds 140 distinct questions
conflicts.statement_a: the filename claims 140 REAL QUESTIONS and 140 items are printed
conflicts.statement_b: 15 of block B’s 102 items reprint a block A item; the fingerprints place 13 cross-block groups and reading both sides confirms the 15 are verbatim, so the file holds 125 distinct constructions
conflicts.why: items 41 and 83 of block B are the SAME block A item printed twice more, so one construction appears three times in one file. A corpus that counted printed items would over-count this source by twelve per cent
conflicts.resolution: NONE. All 140 are coded and the duplicate groups carry the relation; nothing is dropped, because which copy a future reader meets is itself a fact about the source.

conflicts.about: what "REAL" claims for S-017
conflicts.statement_a: the filename asserts real administered questions for all 140
conflicts.statement_b: only block A’s 38 carry an administration tag; block B’s 102 carry no tag, no watermark and no channel annotation of any kind
conflicts.why: provenance is read from content signals, never from a filename (D-1). Block B is the fourth untagged bank block in the corpus and, like the others, it is registered UNKNOWN
conflicts.resolution: NONE. S-016 is recalled_unofficial / OBSERVED, S-017 is unknown / UNKNOWN and NOT_DIRECT_SOURCE. The filename’s claim is recorded, not believed.

conflicts.about: block B’s numbering
conflicts.statement_a: block B is numbered 1 to 104 without a break in the printed sequence
conflicts.statement_b: items 35 and 43 are absent and their slots are printed empty, giving 102 items
conflicts.why: the file’s total reconciles with its filename ONLY because those two gaps cancel: 38 + (104 - 2) = 140. A compilation that had renumbered would have hidden the omission and the count would still have read 140
conflicts.resolution: NONE. Coded as 102 items at their printed ordinals; the gaps are recorded on the S-017 row rather than closed by renumbering.

conflicts.about: item 37 of block A
conflicts.statement_a: the item gives one angle on a transversal of two parallel lines and prints four options
conflicts.statement_b: every angle in that figure is the given angle or its supplement, and neither is among the four printed options
conflicts.why: checkable from the construction alone, which matters because this file prints NO answer key: the defect was found by reading the figure, not by disagreeing with a key. Verified against a 420-dpi render of page 9
conflicts.resolution: NONE. The item is coded on its construction and carries SOURCE_CONFLICT. No answer is invented for it.

conflicts.about: item 66 of block B
conflicts.statement_a: the stem calls the solid a right triangular prism and gives its base area as an expression
conflicts.statement_b: the next two sentences call the same solid a rectangular prism, twice, and the question asks for the surface area of "the right rectangular prism"
conflicts.why: which perimeter the lateral term uses is not settled by the words, so the item has two defensible readings. Unlike item 37 this one cannot be adjudicated from the figure, because there is no figure
conflicts.resolution: NONE. Coded as A-SOL-PRISM-EXPR-SURFACE with competing readings recorded and SOURCE_CONFLICT on the record.

conflicts.about: the figure labels of block A item 19 and its block B reprint, item 104
conflicts.statement_a: the prose names the parallel lines r and s and the transversals t, u and w
conflicts.statement_b: the figure labels those five lines a, b, c, d and e, and the letter d also names one of the marked angles in the prose
conflicts.why: one defect printed twice, which is itself the evidence that item 104 is a reprint rather than a re-authoring. A solver has to guess which "d" the given refers to
conflicts.resolution: NONE. Both copies are coded identically and both carry the note; the mismatch is recorded on the conflict rather than repaired in the record.
